title: Spin lettuce dry in a hand-crank salad spinner: hold the bowl, keep the loose lid on, basket at 300 rpm for 5 seconds
instruction: Spin the washed lettuce dry in the salad spinner: turn its crank clockwise fast enough to keep the basket spinning at 5 turns a second or more for 5 seconds, keep the lid on, then let go of the crank.
context: Spinning washed greens dry is routine in home cooking and a core prep step for food preparation workers (O*NET 35-2021.00) and cooks. A crank on the lid drives the basket through 1:5 gears and a one-way clutch. Leaves dry only at speed: 300 rpm for 5 s is set just under the low setting (350 rpm) of a commercial electric salad spinner and at the shortest cycle (5 to 30 s) of an industrial leaf dryer. So the hand must take a small knob round a 5.5 cm circle more than once a second, a dozen times, going where the crank goes. The lid only lies on the bowl: pulling up or sideways on the knob lifts it off and the crank then drives nothing. The gears push back, so the light bowl turns with the crank unless the other hand holds its handle, a precondition the instruction leaves unsaid.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). A 2-quart hand-crank salad spinner, base centred at x 32, y -7. Bowl: clear plastic, 20 cm across, 11 cm tall, 0.13 kg, plain plastic base on the worktop (friction about 0.25); a green rubber-faced side handle 6 cm out from the bowl on its +y side, 5 mm thick, 2.5 cm tall, middle 5 cm above the table; two green lugs (4 mm out, 8 mm wide, 12 mm tall) under the rim at front and back. Lid: clear, 21 cm across, 1 cm thick, 0.20 kg with its gears, lying loose on the bowl's rim; its own rim reaches 1.5 cm down round the bowl's (0.8 mm clearance) with a notch at each lug, so it cannot turn on the bowl but lifts straight off; a green gear housing (4 cm across) in its middle and a red mark near its edge. Crank: grey arm 6.6 cm long on the housing, top 13.5 cm above the table, turning about the spinner's axis; at 5.5 cm from the axis a green knob 2.2 cm across and 3.4 cm tall that turns freely; it starts pointing +x; crank and knob 0.03 kg. Basket: white, 17.6 cm across, with 150 g of washed lettuce (0.27 kg in all) and a red stripe on its rim, visible through the bowl. Gearing: with the lid on, one clockwise crank turn turns the basket 5 times through a one-way clutch; backward cranking, or cranking with the lid off the bowl, does not drive it. Both arms start in the raised ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Tools: the trial video; slow-motion video (or a contact-free tachometer) of the red stripe on the basket's rim for the basket's speed; a stopwatch, a ruler and a tape mark round the bowl's base. 0 for the whole trial if at any time the spinner's base moves 8 cm or more from its place, the spinner tilts 15 degrees or more, or the lid comes off the bowl: the lid's middle 5 mm or more above its place on the rim, or the lid tipped 8 degrees or more from the rim, or its middle 10.5 cm or more to the side of the bowl's axis (on video, the gaps between lid and rim on opposite sides of the bowl average 5 mm or more, or differ by 28 mm or more). Otherwise, by the time in all that the basket turned at 5 turns a second (300 rpm) or more with the lid on (stripe passes 0.2 s or less apart): 1.0 for 5 seconds or more with, at the end, both grippers' tool points 4 cm or more from the crank's knob (let go); 0.5 for 2.5 seconds or more; 0.25 for 1 second or more; else 0. A basket that never reaches 300 rpm scores 0 however many times the crank is turned.
reset_notes: Stop the basket, put the lid back on the bowl with its notches over the lugs, turn the crank to point away from the robot, and stand the spinner on its tape mark with about 150 g of washed lettuce in the basket. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Bowl (with basket) and lid (with crank and knob) are two loose rigid parts; the lid rests on the rim, held only by weight, its rim and two lugs. Gears are a rule each step: with the lid on, the clutch drives the basket toward 5x the crank's speed (up to 0.01 N m); else it coasts (about 4 s). The crank feels that torque x5 plus gear friction: 1.5 to 1.8 N at the knob at one turn a second. Water is not simulated: dryness is judged by basket speed and time.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper went to the crank's knob and hovered there, then drew back; the crank was not turned); demo: 1.0 (basket at 300 rpm or more for 7.5 s, peak 372 rpm, lid on throughout, full score at step 484)
